takes.h: Ramsey Campbell’s Ancestral listed for November 17 from Flame Tree Press
takes.p: Ramsey Campbell’s novel Ancestral is listed for November 17, 2026, from Flame Tree Press, in hardback and ebook, at 256 pages. In the book’s description, a boy whose parents come from two long-feuding families spends a holiday visiting places both families seem to remember but have never been.

takes.h: Sideshow announces a sixth-scale Regan MacNeil from The Exorcist
takes.p: Sideshow Collectibles opened pre-orders in October for a 1/6-scale Regan MacNeil figure, with release listed for May to August 2027, The Toyark reports. It comes with a fabric nightgown, three pairs of hands and a floating Pazuzu head on a stand. A Deluxe Edition adds two portraits, a four-post bed base and a levitation rod.

Patrick Stewart died on October 28 at his home in Los Angeles, his family said in a statement posted to his Instagram account. He was 86. His horror roles included Dr. Armstrong in Tobe Hooper’s Lifeforce (1985) and Darcy Banker in Jeremy Saulnier’s Green Room (2015).

takes.h: Peter Medak, director of The Changeling, dies at 88
takes.p: Peter Medak died on Tuesday, October 27, in Los Angeles, Dread Central reports, citing Variety. He was 88. His 1980 film The Changeling starred George C. Scott; his horror work also included Species II and episodes of Tales from the Crypt, Masters of Horror and Hannibal.
Vinegar Syndrome has opened a store in Minneapolis, its latest after Bridgeport, Denver, Toronto and Pittsburgh. Blu-ray.com paid a visit.

All three Terrifier films (2016, 2022 and 2024) are back in theaters on consecutive nights around Halloween, presented by Dead by Daylight ahead of Art the Clown's arrival in the game, Rue Morgue reports.

The National Science and Media Museum in Bradford holds the Ashton & Leakey Collection: sketches, prosthetics, glass eyes and fangs from Hammer make-up artists Roy Ashton and Phil Leakey, covering The Curse of Frankenstein (1957), Dracula (1958), The Mummy (1959) and The Gorgon (1964). Great British Life reports the museum is opening the collection up.
